# gdal-bin

**GDAL's command-line tools for rasters and elevation data**

- **Version recorded:** 3.10.3
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://gdal.org/>

## What it does

The Geospatial Data Abstraction Library's programs: `gdalinfo` to inspect a raster, `gdalbuildvrt` to join tiles into one virtual raster, `gdal_contour` to trace contour lines from elevation, `gdal_rasterize` to draw vector data onto a raster, `gdaldem` for hillshade and slope, and many more.

## Why you would want it

It is how `dem-qmapshack` turns the elevation tiles into QMapShack's elevation and contour map, and the standard way to look inside any elevation or map raster yourself.

## Before it will work

None of its own; the tiles come from `dem-copernicus`.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`navigation`](../profiles/navigation.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install gdal-bin --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `gdal-bin`

## Known problems

`gdal_contour` writes into an existing output file rather than refusing it (measured on 3.10.3), so a contour file left from an earlier run is appended to; `dem-qmapshack` removes its own before each run.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
